policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 30:10 reads 'his master'. Qere אֲדֹנָ֑יו and ketiv אדנו differ only as plural-of-majesty against singular suffix, and both are rendered by a singular English 'his master'; the ASV carries no note here. Nothing in the English distinguishes the readings, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV 30:18 reads 'Yea, four which I know not'. Qere וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה and ketiv וארבע differ only in the gender form of the numeral 'four'; English numerals carry no gender, so both yield 'four' and no ASV note is mapped here. Underdetermined, with the qere base fallback retained.
